Method of Attack: Linux malware toolset consisting of an implant client coupled with a kernel module rootkit, a file transfer and port forwarding tool, and a Command and Control (C2) server
Executes arbitrary commands with root privileges
Forwards network traffic to other machines
Kernel module rootkit that hides on infected machines and survives reboots unless UEFI secure boot is enabled in Full or Thorough mode
Communicates via JSON over WebSockets with encrypted traffic using RSA algorithm
Impacted Systems: Linux systems with kernel version below 3.7 or without UEFI Secure Boot enabled
Attack Vector: Exploitation of systems without secure boot or kernel signing enforcement
Indicators of Compromise: IP addresses and ports used in lab analysis (not from live operations)
Specific filenames, paths, hashes, Yara rules, and Snort rules provided in NSA report
Network traffic patterns identifiable by NIDS like Suricata, Snort, Zeek via de-obfuscation of WebSocket messages
